clue.text: Swimmers used to be trained in West

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters sit inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West, the American film star

indicators.note: letters that are to be trained are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A note that people who swim used to be coached in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a compass point, but it is the film star Mae West, whose first name holds the letters 'to be trained' makes of 'used'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusae are jellyfish in their free-swimming form, so they are swimmers of the sea.

clue.text: Married girl's animus

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The hostility harboured by a married young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of girl's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus means hostile intent or ill will, a synonym.

clue.text: List the best finally entering parliament

indicators.note: entering says those closing letters go inside the parliament's name

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the words the and best

explanation.surface: An instruction to list the finest people at last getting into parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The parliament is Ireland's, the Dáil; 'finally' acts on both 'the' and 'best', and 'entering' puts the pair inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things is to itemise or set them out one by one, a verb synonym.

clue.text: You and my sons oddly retain name that's closely associated

indicators.note: retain says the shuffled letters hold another letter within them
oddly says the letters of the words are arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: A parent remarks that you and their sons strangely keep a name with close ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' scrambles YOU MY SONS, and 'retain' has those letters hold N.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are synonyms have closely associated meanings, being alike in sense.

clue.text: Look briefly across stage for exit lines

indicators.note: across says the shortened word stretches either side of the stage
briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an eye is a look, as in 'cast an eye over'
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A glance at the stage while an actor departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the last letter and 'across' spreads what is left round the stage. 'exit lines' sound theatrical, but the exit is death.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem of mourning is written for someone who has died, so it is lines on their exit from life.

clue.text: Bush, a murderer, right at the top

indicators.note: at the top says one letter is taken to the front of the assassin's name

parts.note: Brutus was one of the assassins of Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A political jibe calling President Bush a killer, with a right-wing slant on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the president; it is the plant. Brutus was Caesar's assassin, and 'at the top' shifts his name's R to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus, or strawberry tree, is an evergreen shrub, so an example of a bush.

clue.text: Doing seller's job out of uniform

indicators.note: out of says a letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: an auctioneer sells by auctioning
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone doing a salesperson's work without wearing the uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes U from AUCTIONING.
explanation.definitionFit: Actioning is office jargon for carrying out a task, so it means doing.

clue.text: Attractive girl in black Lincoln

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Abe Lincoln, the American president

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman in a black Lincoln car.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is slang for a good-looking young woman.

clue.text: Rubbish "politician" stuffs more balanced adversary, finally

indicators.note: stuffs says the politician is packed inside the other letters

parts.note: a truer wheel or beam is more evenly balanced
MP, Member of Parliament

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of adversary

explanation.surface: A dig at a rubbish politician who outdoes a fairer opponent, with Trump the obvious target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives Y, the end of 'adversary', and MP 'stuffs' TRUERY. The quotes round 'politician' nod to Donald Trump, whose name the answer opens with.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery is showy but worthless stuff, nonsense, so it means rubbish.

clue.text: Watch patient eating date capsule

parts.note: to watch is to see
a case is a patient in a doctor's care

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on a hospital patient eating a date from its capsule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts D inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed case is the pod or capsule that holds a plant's seeds.

clue.text: Chunk of congenitally revolting tongue

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the run is read backwards
a chunk of a word is a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Part of something inborn that is disgusting to the taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chunk of' takes NITAL from 'congenitally' and 'revolting' turns it round. 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting'; it means turning back.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and the language of ancient Rome is one.

clue.text: European races pig round hairpin — famous last words

parts.note: the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
a hairpin bend is U-shaped
a pig, as an insult, is a brute

explanation.surface: A European motorcyclist hurtles round a hairpin bend on the TT course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' links the pig to the hairpin bend it goes round: U comes before BRUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's dying reproach to Brutus in Shakespeare is among the best-known final utterances.

clue.text: Played hymn to 12 that's on top of stack

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: the solution to 12 across, a word for grand on a huge scale

explanation.surface: A hymn is performed for a grand occasion on top of a pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' rearranges HYMN TO with EPIC, the answer to 12.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney stack carries a pot on top as the outlet for smoke.

clue.text: Nice grocer's offloading water on a huge scale

indicators.note: offloading says a part of the French word is dropped

parts.note: in Nice, in France, a grocer's shop is an épicerie
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A pleasant grocer unloads a huge amount of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offloading' removes ERIE from EPICERIE. 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant'; it is the French city, so the shop is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand, heroic or vast in scale.

clue.text: Oversupply a couple's food additives

parts.note: a glut is an oversupply
read as the verb couples: to couple is to mate

explanation.surface: Too much of a pair's share of food additives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple's' reads as the verb 'couples', which is MATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutamates such as MSG are flavour enhancers added to food.

clue.text: Old satirist begins shedding stone in judo etc

parts.note: Martial was a Roman poet of satirical epigrams

indicators.note: shedding says letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: begins means starts
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: An ancient satirist starts losing weight by taking up judo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding' removes ST from STARTS. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo, karate and the like are combat sports, examples of the category.

clue.text: Improving picture: judge and artist reach China

parts.note: ref, referee, is a judge in sport
RA, Royal Academician
Ming is a dynasty of China, and its porcelain

explanation.surface: A judge and a painter get to China to make a picture better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but the Ming porcelain is the china meant; 'and' and 'reach' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Reframing a picture, giving it a new frame, can be done to improve it; the verb form fits.

clue.text: Forerunner of 9 puzzled centaurs

indicators.note: puzzled says the letters are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: Mythical half-horse creatures are baffled by an ancestor of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscan civilisation and its tongue preceded Latin, the answer to 9, in Italy.

clue.text: Article on speed or rate occasionally jars

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of rate

explanation.surface: An article about speed or rate sometimes grates on the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives A and E, alternate letters of 'rate'. 'jars' looks like a verb; it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphorae are tall two-handled pottery vessels of the ancient world, a kind of jar.

clue.text: Doctor must get up, if time's at a premium

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A medic must rise when time is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person; as a verb it rearranges MUST GET UP IF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means time flies, so time is short and precious.

clue.text: Old queen chopping vegetables works in Covent Garden

indicators.note: chopping says the queen cuts into the vegetables

parts.note: peas are vegetables
R, regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An elderly queen chops vegetables at the London fruit and vegetable market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping' puts R inside PEAS. Covent Garden is a London district, once its main produce market, and home of the Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical dramas are the works staged at the Royal Opera House in Covent Garden.

clue.text: Studies eastern and southern states

parts.note: to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: Research into the eastern and southern American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like US states; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A study can be a short written piece examining a subject, as an essay is.

clue.text: Hacks ignore firm making disapproving noises

indicators.note: ignore says part of the word is left out

parts.note: a hack is a dry cough
CO, company, is a firm

explanation.surface: Journalists ignore a company and make grunts of disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignore' removes CO from COUGHS. 'Hacks' looks like journalists; it is coughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugh is an interjection of disgust, so these are sounds of distaste.

clue.text: Bubbly soup needs work, significant work

parts.note: a magnum is a large bottle of champagne

indicators.note: needs work says the word must be reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A cook's verdict: the champagne soup needs more effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs work' rearranges SOUP into OPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum opus is a person's greatest achievement, their most important creation.

clue.text: Water sources current doctor found in province

indicators.note: found in says the pieces sit inside the province's letters

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, the UK province
I is the symbol for electric current
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Supplies of water and electricity, and a doctor, in a province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places IMB inside NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain clouds, from which water falls.

clue.text: House section of cruise missile

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A building is part of a cruise missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, a British home sharing one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Fish go in mid-December, so strike now!

parts.note: a carp is a fish

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
mid- picks the central letters of the month's name

parts.note: to go is to die

explanation.surface: Fishing in mid-December, an angler is told to cast now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-' takes the central pair of letters of 'December', and 'in' sets the word for go between them. 'strike' is an angler's word here, but the motto means act now.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horace motto urges seizing the day, so it calls for acting at once.

clue.text: Old soldiers hiding blunder land in 9

indicators.note: hiding says the reserve conceals another word within it

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, the former British army reserve
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: Veterans cover up a mistake made on foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve, and 'hiding' has it hold the blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for earth or ground; 9 is the solution LATIN.

clue.text: Short of bakery job, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving another of the same sound

parts.note: a baker works dough, kneading it

explanation.surface: Lacking work in a bakery, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the baker's word is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in want of something is lacking it, so the phrase means requiring.

clue.text: Stylish novices rebuffing leading lady's demands

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: rebuffing says the novices turn away, so letters are removed

parts.note: novices in a convent are sisters
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Fashionable newcomers snub the star actress, who makes demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffing' drops ER from SISTERS. 'leading lady' looks like a star actress; it is the Queen, ER. The 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb insists means presses for something firmly, as demands does.
